answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table due to the non-revertible security patch, and regional failover risks in-flight writes during the settlement peak. Write-path latency climbing at peak write load points to capacity saturation rather than a dependency failure (circuit breaker) or read contention (replica routing won't help a write-path problem). Memory_b3 supports provisioning headroom to absorb load; memory_b5 cautions against routing-reads since this is write-side; memory_b6 suggests the new release may contribute, but since it can't be reverted, adding capacity is the lever that preserves writes and availability without touching the mandated release. Scaling writes is reversible and low-risk.
